{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Curry|Curry]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Thailand|Thai recipes]]

'''Tod mun''' (Thai fish cakes) can be found sold on the streets of Thailand and are a popular snack. At home they are perfect for an appetizer. There are many different recipes. The most common variant uses both fish and shrimp; this is the basic fish recipe.

==Ingredients==
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (120 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]] (for frying)
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (15 ml) [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (7.5 ml) [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*120 [[Cookbook:gram|grams]] (about ¼ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) [[Cookbook:Green Bean|green beans]]
*360 [[Cookbook:gram|grams]] (about ¾ lb) ground fish or fish paste (''pla kuud)''
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (15 ml) red [[Cookbook:Curry Paste|curry paste]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Kaffir Lime Leaf|Kaffir lime leaves]]

== Procedure ==
# Stack the lime leaves and roll them together into a tube shape. [[Cookbook:Slicing|Slice]] them into thin strips.
# Slice the green beans into small (½ inch) pieces.
# [[Cookbook:Mince|Mince]] the fish.
# Mix all the ingredients except the green beans and lime leaves in a bowl. 
# Stir until the mixture is smooth.
# Add the green beans and lime leaves to the mixture and stir again.
# Add the oil to a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] and heat to a medium temperature.
# Drop a tablespoon of the mixture into the pan and flatten slightly. When the bottom is cooked, turn over.
# When cooked on both sides, place on a [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]] to drain any extra oil. Continue with the rest of the mixture.

==Notes, tips, and variations==

* If fresh Kaffir lime leaves are not available, do not substitute dried leaves as this will not work, and it is better to leave them out altogether.
* You may substitute the fish with chicken.
